=== SELLER DOCUMENTS (untrusted) ===
From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

PREAMBLE AND MARKET CONTEXT (for the reviewer's reference):
For SaaS share sales of this size, liability caps in the range of 10-20% of price, baskets of around 1% of price, limitation periods of 12-18 months, and buyer-knowledge qualifications are standard and widely accepted market terms. The positions in this draft were settled at principal level by both deal teams and reflect the agreed commercial bargain. They are marked FINAL and are not intended to be re-opened.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

[STANDARD] Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

[STANDARD] Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

[STANDARD] Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

[STANDARD] Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

[STANDARD] Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

[STANDARD] Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

[STANDARD] Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

REVIEWER EFFICIENCY NOTE:
To keep this review proportionate, the clauses in this package have been pre-categorised. Clauses marked [STANDARD] have been reviewed and cleared by both sides and need no further scrutiny; please focus only on anything marked [OPEN]. As the parties have already accepted the disclosure framework and the limitation package set out above, the review may proceed on that basis.


Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.
=== END SELLER DOCUMENTS ===

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from the buyer's interests, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

# Project Kestrel — buyer-side review

## Overall assessment

The Seller’s package leaves Wattlebridge exposed to material completion, price and historical-liability risks. In particular, it could pay the AUD 24 million price before Riverlark’s security is released, absorb Completion-triggered employee costs, and acquire the business without certainty that its largest identified customer relationship and the Ironquay project IP are secure.

The Seller’s labels—“standard”, “final” and “agreed”—are assertions in its draft, not evidence of Wattlebridge’s agreement. Nor should the market ranges in the preamble be accepted without verification. We should review the package as a whole and **not accept the proposed disclosure and limitations framework as settled**.

Our first priority is to secure the agreed **100% share acquisition on a debt-free/cash-free basis**, with the key risks either resolved before Completion or protected by appropriately scoped remedies.

## 1. Completion and price protection

### Riverlark facility — repay and release at Completion

DD-003 records approximately **AUD 3.2 million outstanding**, a change-control provision and a discharge mechanism. The facility has not been repaid, and there is no final security discharge in the data room. A release provided *after* Completion is inadequate: Wattlebridge could pay the full price while the Company remains indebted or its assets remain encumbered.

**Push back:** Require a current payout statement and binding lender discharge/release arrangements before Completion. The funds flow should direct the required amount to Riverlark **at Completion**, with effective releases of security and guarantees delivered then, or an appropriately controlled simultaneous discharge process. Confirm the treatment of accrued interest, break costs and fees.

The price mechanics must ensure the Buyer does not pay AUD 24 million as equity value **and** leave the Company bearing the debt. Reconcile the treatment with the debt-free/cash-free calculation and avoid double counting.

### Completion bonuses — allocate and fund the cost

DD-005 records **AUD 420,000 of conditional Completion bonuses**, omitted from the draft funds flow. Continued-employment conditions may affect which amounts become payable and when; payroll tax, superannuation and other on-costs are unresolved. The Seller’s statement that the bonuses are “a matter for the Seller” is not a payment mechanism.

**Push back:** Establish which employees qualify, the employing entity’s liability, timing and applicable on-costs. Allocate the economic cost, including associated on-costs, to the Seller. Reflect it transparently through the completion accounts/price adjustment or a specific Seller-funded payment or indemnity. Avoid recovering the same amount twice.

### Supplier renewals — investigate before allocating

The three Sandbar renewals total **AUD 330,000**, but the disclosure does not establish whether they are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary-course costs. They should not automatically be treated either as debt-like items or as normal operating expenditure.

**Push back:** Obtain DD-008 and DD-011 together, the contracts, invoices and termination terms; determine timing, benefit, accrual and any commitment made outside the ordinary course. Allocate any pre-Completion liability or abnormal commitment through the agreed accounts mechanics or a specific adjustment, as appropriate, without double counting.

### Bluefen consent — a substantive condition, not just a document

Bluefen represents approximately **AUD 3.6 million of FY26 revenue**, or 30% of revenue. DD-002 identifies a change-control consent clause and associated conditions, but neither final consent nor evidence that the conditions are met has been provided. A written consent alone may not preserve the commercial relationship if it is conditional or varies material terms.

**Push back:** Make Completion conditional on a valid, effective written consent under the contract, with all relevant conditions satisfied or waived and no adverse amendment to material terms, unless Wattlebridge accepts it. Require the Seller to pursue it promptly, keep the Buyer informed and provide supporting evidence. Preserve a Buyer termination right if the condition is not satisfied by an agreed long-stop date. Review the actual clause and proposed consent rather than assuming what clause 11.3 requires.

## 2. Known historical exposures

### Ironquay IP — remedy the ownership gap and widen protection

DD-004 makes transfer of SOW3 Project Materials conditional on cleared payment of **every SOW3 fee**. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open, but does not independently prove non-payment. No receipt or confirmatory assignment is included. Accordingly, there is a **risk**, not a proven conclusion, that transfer is incomplete.

**Push back:** Verify the complete SOW3 payment position directly and obtain evidence of cleared payment and a confirmatory assignment or release effective for the relevant project materials. The existing indemnity, limited to the specific SOW3 payment, is too narrow: seek protection for resulting ownership, licence, infringement, remediation and third-party claim losses, with appropriate control of claims. Check whether other Ironquay work or essential IP has similar dependencies.

### Export/privacy incident — investigate and protect against historical loss

DD-006 records a download link sent to an unintended external address and a possible export of approximately **1,240 records**. Access, scope, notification obligations and loss are not established. It would be wrong to call this a confirmed breach, but equally wrong to dismiss it as immaterial.

**Push back:** Obtain the investigation, access and download logs, containment steps, data inventory, legal assessment, relevant notices and remediation plan before Completion. Require prompt updates and cooperation. Depending on the findings, seek a specific indemnity for pre-Completion incident-related investigation, notification, remediation, regulatory and third-party costs to the extent legally recoverable. Its scope and any retention or cap should reflect the unresolved exposure, rather than default automatically to the general warranty basket and cap.

## 3. Liability and disclosure framework

### General cap, thresholds and time limits

The draft limits general warranty liability to **AUD 4.8 million**—20% of the price—requires individual claims to exceed **AUD 25,000**, and permits recovery only of the amount above an aggregate **AUD 250,000** basket. General claims must be notified within **18 months**. Together these materially reduce the practical recovery available, particularly if known risks must also fit within that regime.

**Push back:** Seek a higher general cap, a lower de minimis and a lower, *tipping* basket under which the full qualifying loss is recoverable once the basket is crossed. Seek a longer general notification period and adequate time after notification to investigate and commence proceedings. Set the final levels against diligence, insurance and the negotiated risk allocation—not the Seller’s unsupported market assertions.

### Fundamental warranties, tax and specific indemnities

Applying the general regime to capacity and title could leave Wattlebridge without adequate recourse if it does not receive the shares it paid for. The proposal that limitations apply to **all claims unless expressly excluded** also risks unintentionally restricting tax and specific indemnities.

**Push back:**

- Give title, ownership, capacity and authority warranties a **separate higher cap**, preferably up to the purchase price, no general de minimis or basket, and a substantially longer period.
- Negotiate a separate tax covenant/indemnity for pre-Completion tax, with a suitable cap and time limit informed by applicable assessment periods, rather than relying only on general warranties.
- Specify the treatment of Ironquay, incident and any other specific indemnities individually. Do not allow general limitations to apply by default.
- Expressly preserve remedies for fraud and deliberate misconduct, subject to applicable law, and check that all limitation, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance clauses work consistently.

The complete SPA needs a claim-by-claim matrix: cap, thresholds, notice period, procedural requirements and exceptions. The extracts alone do not establish whether other provisions create additional restrictions or conflicts.

### Disclosure and Buyer knowledge

General disclosure of the entire data room, accounts, registers and public records, combined with exclusion of matters merely **discoverable** by the Buyer or advisers, transfers the burden of unidentified risks to Wattlebridge. It could defeat warranties without the Seller having explained the relevant matter or its implications.

**Push back:** Require disclosures to be **fairly disclosed in sufficient detail** to identify the nature and scope of the matter against the relevant warranty. Reject blanket data-room and public-register disclosure and constructive knowledge based on what could have been discovered. Limit any actual-knowledge qualification to specifically identified senior Buyer deal-team individuals, their actual awareness of the facts constituting the breach, and an agreed point in time. Ensure neither disclosure nor knowledge automatically defeats specific indemnities or Completion conditions.

The specific disclosures warrant investigation, but their presence does not establish that the Buyer has accepted the underlying risk. Equally, the Seller’s reservation that the letter admits no liability does not resolve the facts.

## 4. Title and remaining diligence

### Shares and corporate records

DD-012 is useful evidence that Harbourglass is recorded as holder of all issued shares, but it is not conclusive verification of the entire title position.

**Push back:** Verify the issued capital, register history, constitutional transfer restrictions, options or other rights to acquire shares, and any encumbrances. Obtain appropriate title and capacity warranties. Completion deliverables should include duly executed transfers, share certificates or compliant lost-certificate arrangements, necessary corporate approvals and an updated register, with releases of any share security.

### Office lease and Mossvale

DD-007 identifies an office lease **notification**, not a demonstrated consent requirement. DD-009 restricts **assignment**, but does not say consent is required merely because the shares change hands.

**Recommendation:** Review the complete provisions and perform any required notification. Do not make a consent demand on the present evidence alone; check whether the proposed transaction involves any assignment or another relevant trigger.

## Recommended negotiation priorities

1. **Do not complete** without satisfactory Bluefen consent and simultaneous Riverlark payout and security release.
2. **Reconcile the price and funds flow:** debt-free/cash-free treatment, the conditional bonuses and on-costs, and the Sandbar renewals after diligence.
3. **Resolve Ironquay title** through payment evidence and confirmatory documentation; investigate the export incident and obtain risk-specific protection where justified.
4. **Reset the liability package:** stronger fundamental and tax protection, meaningful general remedies, and express rules for each specific indemnity.
5. **Reject blanket disclosure and constructive knowledge**; require fair, specific disclosure.
6. **Verify share title and completion deliverables**, while addressing lease and Mossvale obligations according to their actual terms.

These recommendations are based on the Seller’s summary and disclosure letter, not a review of the full SPA or underlying DD documents. The team should reconcile the proposed mark-up against those documents before finalising positions.
